set.st: On 24 July 1933 a posse surprised the Barrow gang camped on the wooded hill above Dexfield Park. Buck Barrow was mortally wounded and Blanche Barrow captured; Clyde Barrow, Bonnie Parker and W. D. Jones escaped. Forum tellings say up to $65,000 in loot was buried near the camp. No period record of any cache has been found, and the gang's known takings were far smaller. Pin circle (400 m) is on 'The Dexfield Park Co.' tract of the 1916 county atlas, the S part of sec. 7 with the river as its north edge; not the spot itself.
set.t: The shootout is well documented; the loot is not. Period papers for 25-31 July 1933 (Dexter, Adel, Des Moines) are being read for what money was found on the gang. On the 1930 aerial the tract is a clearing with a cluster of buildings on the south bank, with wooded rises to the south where the gang camped. No digging; look-only.
pinev: Dexfield Park Co. tract, S part sec. 7 T78N R29W, river as N edge (1916 Dallas Co atlas); first sec. 17/18 reading withdrawn. Checked on the 1930 ortho: the pin is on the south bank in the park clearing, not in the river.

tw-mn-henderson-ritter-beer-casks.t: An Enes family was in Henderson from the 1870s (John Enes, born 1828 Prussia, and sons), so an 'Enes brewery' is plausible but not yet proven; Joseph Ritter is the only brewer in the 1870 and 1880 census.
